name: Dumbbells Only
description:
12-Week Dumbbell-Only Muscle Builder

Who It's For: If you're tight on time and equipment but big on muscle-building ambitions, this 12-week dumbbell-only plan is your ideal fit. Perfect for anyone with a pair of dumbbells and a drive to see real results.

Equipment Needed: Just a few pairs of dumbbells. Nothing more, nothing less.

Plan Overview:

Frequency: 4 full-body workouts per week.

Progressive Intensity: We start off easy, then gradually ramp up the intensity each week. This ensures you comfortably adapt to more challenging workouts, setting your muscles up for unprecedented growth.

What to Expect:

Supersets Galore: As you progress, get ready for supersets – back-to-back exercises with zero rest, designed to maximize your workout efficiency.

Advanced Techniques: Along the journey, you'll encounter various high-intensity training methods that'll push your limits and supercharge your gains.

Training Philosophy:

Efficient Workouts: When time is scarce, intensity becomes your best friend. This program is designed to make the most out of every workout.
Smooth Progression: We'll slowly dial up the intensity, so you'll barely notice how hard you're working – until you see the results.
Get ready to embark on a journey of efficient, effective muscle building. Grab your dumbbells, and let's make those gains happen!

blocks.label: Weeks 1-4 · straight sets · 4010 tempo
blocks.intro:
The first 4 Weeks we`re doing every exercise with a 4010 Tempo, which just means you're lowering the weight ( or yourself ) for 4 seconds and go up like you would normally.

Take at least one big step away from the box or bench you're using to elevate your rear leg.
Try staying as upright as possible while shifting your weight onto your front leg.
Go all the way down until your knee touches the floor and go all the way back up.

If you can, hold onto something with your free hand for more stability.
Tempo: 4010
Intensity: 9/10

Start with the weight touching your chest and your upper arms in a 45 degree angle.
Bring the weight all the way up, until the elbows are fully extended and hands are above the shoulder.
Slowly bring the weight back in the starting position and there you got your first rep!
Tempo: 4010
Intensity: 9/10

Start with straight arms and hands directly above your shoulders.
Bring the weight slowly down until it's next to your torso, while keeping the elbows slightly bent.
Enjoy the stretch and slowly bring the weight back up through squeezing your chest.
Tempo: 4010
Intensity: 9/10

The non working arm is on the bench, and the knee on this side as well.
Let the working arm fully extend and bring your shoulder forward.
From there try to pull your arm back towards your hip and slowly bring it down again.
Tempo: 4010
Intensity: 9/10
Perform Each Side

Make sure the upper arm stays straight - so elbows are always pointing to the ceiling.
Only the forearms are moving. Bring your hands all the way down until the Dumbbell touches your shoulder and fully extend your elbows at the top.

Start seated with a dumbbell in each hand.
Palms are facing forwards, know bend at the elbows and bring the weight up to your shoulder.
You want as little movement in the upper arm as possible and keep them close to your torso.
Tempo: 4010
Intensity: 10/10

Use small plates to elevate your heels, to get more tension in your quads.

Make sure to push your elbows inwards at all times, while holding the dumbbell as close to your chest as possible. When going down, let your knees travel forward and out while trying to stay as upright as possible.
Tempo: 4010
Intensity: 9/10

Start in a standing position ehile having a dumbbell in each hand.
Push your glutes as far back as possible, while keeping the elbows locked.
Keep your chest out and back straight, while avoiding bending the knees too much.
Tempo: 4010
Intensity: 9/10

Start standing nice and tall with a proud chest.
Holding one dumbbell on top of your shoulder.
Press it all the way up above your head and slowly bring it down again.

Start with your weaker arm ( often it's the left side for right handed individuals ) 
and just match the reps with the other side - avoid doing more on one side
Tempo: 4010
Intensity: 9/10
Perform Each Side

Keep your elbows slightly bent, here it's not just about bringing the weight up - it's more like pushing the weights away from your body. Try to create as much tension as possible in your shoulders.
Tempo: 4010
Intensity: 10/10

Bend over like you would in a RDL, let your arms hang loose.
From there bring the weight out to the side and pull your shoulderblades together ( proud chest )
Try to avoid working with your neck.
Tempo: 4010
Intensity: 10/10

Get as Many Reps as you can! And if you think you can't go anymore - do at least 5 more!

blocks.label: Weeks 5-8 · supersets · 3012 / 3210 tempo
blocks.intro:
The next four weeks we're doing a 3012/ 3210 Tempo, which means you're doing the negative for 3 seconds, go up like you usually would and hold for 2 seconds at the point where it's the toghest.
I.e.: Hip thrust and row you hold at the top, dumbbell press you stop at the bottom.

Right after the first set you go straight into the walking lunges and then you have alonger break, 
after that you start with hip thrusts again.

Make sure only your shoulderblades are on top of the box / bench you're using
The Dumbbell should be on your belt line. Make sure your heels are at least one foot-length away from your glute.
If you're standing to close you'll mainly feel your quad, if you're standing too far away you'll feel it more in you hamstrings.
To know the perfect distance, if you're watching from the side: your upper/lower leg should be at a 90 degree angle in the top position.

If you have trouble feeling your glute and always feel it in your back, you're probably overextending your back. There's a simple trick to avoid that: Put your chin on your chest and only go so high that you still can see your knees.
Tempo: 3012
Intensity: 9/10

Make sure to stay as upright as you can while doing the steps.
You can also start with just bodyweight and add a little weight from week to week.

You don't need to take tempo into account here, but make sure to do controlled movements.

After the 2min rest period you start with hip thrusts again.
Intensity: 10/10

The next four weeks we're doing a 3012/ 3210 Tempo, which means you're doing the negative for 3 seconds, here you hold at the bottom for 2s and then press up like usual.

After the first set you go directly into the pushups, rep out the set and then rest 2min.
Then start with the dumbbell press again and to the same thing.

Start with the weight touching your chest and your upper arms in a 45 degree angle.
Bring the weight all the way up, until the elbows are fully extended and hands are above the shoulder.
Slowly bring the weight back in the starting position and there you got your first rep!
Tempo: 3210
Intensity: 9/10

Start with your hands slightly wider than shoulder width and hands in one line with your shoulders.
From there bring yourself slowly down, while keeping the elbows close to your torso.
From there bring it up more explosively until you're back in the starting Position.
Shoulders should be as far away from your Ears as possible.
Tempo: 3210
Intensity: 10/10

The next four weeks we're doing a 3012/ 3210 Tempo, which means you're doing the negative for 3 seconds, here you hold at the top for 2s and then go down like usual.

After the first set you go directly into the rows, rep out the set and then rest 2min.
Then start with the dumbbell lateral raise again and to the row again and so on.

Lie down on an incline bench with your belly on the backrest, a weight in each hand.
Let your arms fully extend and bring your shoulders forward.
From there try to pull your arms to your side. 
That's right, i said pull. You're moving the weights through pulling your shoulderblades together.
Tempo: 3012
Intensity: 10/10

Start with an incline bench and lay down with your belly on the pad, a weight in each hand.
Let your arms fully extend and bring your shoulders forward.
From there try to pull your elbows back towards your belly button and squeeze the upper back.
Hold for a second and slowly bring the weight down again.
Tempo: 3012
Intensity: 9/10

First do weaker leg, then the other leg, then move on to the goblet squat, rest 2 minutes and start with the step ups again.

You don't need to take the tempo into account here, but do controlled movements,
especially on the negative.

Stand directly in front of the box and put one foot on it.
Try staying as upright as possible while shifting your weight onto your front leg.
Push yourself up all the way up until the working leg is completely straight , thengo all the way back down. Finish all reps of that set and swith legs.
Tempo: 3012
Intensity: 9/10
Perform Each Side

The next four weeks we're doing a 3012/ 3210 Tempo, which means you're doing the negative for 3 seconds, here you hold at the bottom for 2s and then go up like usual.

Use small plates to elevate your heels, to get more tension in your quads.

Make sure to push your elbows inwards at all times, while holding the dumbbell as close to your chest as possible. When going down, let your knees travel forward and out while trying to stay as upright as possible.
Tempo: 3210
Intensity: 10/10

After the first set you go directly into the front raises, rep out the set and then rest 2min.
Then start with the dumbbell press again and to the same thing.

Start with the weight touching your shoulders and your upper arms in a 45 degree angle.
Bring the weight all the way up, until the elbows are fully extended above your head so shoulder, elbow and hands should be in one line.
Slowly bring the weight back in the starting position and there you got your first rep!
Tempo: 3210
Intensity: 9/10

Start standing with a dumbbell in each hand.
Raise them in front of you to shoulder height without bending at the elbows.
Start light here and focus on feeling your shoulder work.
Tempo: 3012
Intensity: 10/10

After the first set you rest 1 minute, then go to the tricep exercise, do the set, rest 1 minute again and do the curls again. So you're switching back and forth between those two, but with rest in between.

Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Curl the weights up towards your shoulder, without any movement in the upper arm.
Tempo: 3012
Intensity: 10/10

The next four weeks we're doing a 3012/ 3210 Tempo, which means you're doing the negative for 3 
seconds, here you hold at the bottom for 2s and then press up like usual.

Make sure your upper arm stays locked next to your ear at all times, only forearms are moving.
Tempo: 3210
Intensity: 10/10

Now we're doing MAX REPS here, get as many as in until you can't go anymore....And then do some more!

Do one set of 60 reps, no matter how long it takes or how often you need to rest in between ... just get them in.

blocks.label: Weeks 9-12 · tri-sets
blocks.intro:
The next 4 Weeks we're doing Tri-sets, so 3 exercises in a row.
Prepare yourself to push yourself mentally and make your muscles burn ( and grow of course )

Theres no prescribed tempo but still make sure to control the weight and not let the weight control you.

Use small plates under your heels to shift some more of the tension towards your quads.
Feet should be hip width apart and toes pointing outwards slightly.
Make sure to push the knees outwards and forwards.
Hold the dumbbell as close to your chest as possible.

It's basically the same movement as an RDL, but you bend your knees just a little bit less.
That way you shift more tension towards your hamstrings.
So Push your glutes back while keeping your legs a bit straighter than usual.
Still make sure to keep your back straight and your chest proud.
Intensity: 9/10

Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, take a big step backwards and go down until the knee reaches the floor. Goal is to stay as upright as you can while doing your reps. 
Go back up and do the same thing with the other leg.
Intensity: 10/10
Perform Each Side

Start with the weight touching your shoulders and your upper arms close to your torso,
so weight and elbows are in one straight line, pointing upwards.
Bring the weight all the way up, until the elbows are fully extended above your head so shoulder, elbow and hands are in one line.
Slowly bring the weight back in the starting position and there you got your first rep!
Intensity: 9/10

Make sure only the forearms are moving, elbows are pointing to the ceiling.
Start with your arms fully extended like the end position of a dumbbell press, bring the dumbbells all the way down to your shoulder without the upper arm changing it's position. When you touch your shoulder bring it all the way back up until the arms are fully extended.
No swinging!
Intensity: 9/10

Start standing with a dumbbell in each hand. Keep your elbows slightly bent, here it's not just about bringing the weight up - it's more like pushing the weights away from your body. Bring them up to shoulder height and then slowly go down again.
Try to create as much tension as possible in your shoulders.
Intensity: 10/10

Start standing with a dumbbell in each hand. Curl them up like usual, BUT at the top turn your hands around so your palms are facing the floor. Go down very slow and controlled.
Next rep should start like a regular curl again.

So on the way up, palms are facing up. On the way down palms are facing down.
Intensity: 9/10

Stand with a dumbbell in each hand and curl them up with your palms facing upwards.
Upper arm shouldn't move at all always be in contact with your torso.
Intensity: 10/10

Lie down on the bench, with just one dumbbell you hold with both of your hands, directly above your face. Now slowly start bringing the dumbbell backwards above your head.
Make yourself as long as possible , elbows are slightly bent, and they stay like that the whole time!
Go down until your upper arms are next to your ears and you feel a nice stretch in your lats.
Now use your lat to slowly bring your hands upwards again.
The movement should look like a curve from the side.
Intensity: 9/10

Start with an incline bench and lay down with your belly on the pad, a weight in each hand.
Let your arms fully extend and bring your shoulders forward.
From there try to pull your arms back towards your belly button and squeeze the upper back.
Hold for a second and slowly bring the weight down again.
Intensity: 10/10

Start with straight arms and hands directly above your shoulders.
Bring the weight slowly down until it's next to your torso, while keeping the elbows slightly bent.
Enjoy the stretch and slowly bring the weight back up through squeezing your chest.
Intensity: 9/10

Start with the weight touching your chest and your upper arms in a 45 degree angle.
Bring the weight all the way up, until the elbows are fully extended and hands are above the shoulder.
Slowly bring the weight back in the starting position and there you got your first rep!
Intensity: 9/10

Last week it was okay to start a little easier, make sure to PUSH HARD this week!

Take at least one big step away from the box or bench you're using to elevate your rear leg.
Try staying as upright as possible while shifting your weight onto your front leg.
Go all the way down until your knee touches the floor and go all the way back up.

Try to always do the same amount of reps on each side.
Intensity: 10/10
Perform Each Side

Start with the weight touching your shoulders and your upper arms at 45 degrees,
Bring the weight all the way up, until the elbows are fully extended above your head so shoulder, elbow and hands are in one line.
Slowly bring the weight back in the starting position and there you got your first rep!
Intensity: 9/10

 Go down very slow and controlled.

Bend over like you would in a RDL, let your arms hang loose.
From there bring the weight out to the side and pull your shoulderblades together ( proud chest )
Try to avoid working with your neck.

Intensity: 9/10

exercises.name: Walking DB Lunge
exercises.instruction:
GO ALL OUT! Go until you can't no more and then go on.

Nice and controlled reps, make sure to stay upright.

Intensity: 9/10

exercises.instruction: Go as HARD as you can!

exercises.name: Double Dumbbell Overhead Extension (Seated)
exercises.instruction:
GO ALL OUT!

Make sure only the forearms are moving, elbows are pointing to the ceiling.
Bring the dumbbells all the way down to your shoulder without the upper arm changing it's position.
 When you touch your shoulder bring it all the way back up until the arms are fully extended.

Intensity: 9/10
